title: PerspectiveCamera
sub: Field of view, aspect, near and far
cards/0/body:
A camera sees a truncated pyramid called the frustum. Four numbers define it:

fov: the vertical field of view in degrees.
aspect: frame width ÷ height.
near: nothing closer than this is drawn.
far: nothing farther than this is drawn either.
cards/1/task: The green cube sits off to the side and is out of frame. Widen the view without moving the camera.
cards/2/q: What does a large fov, say 100, do?
cards/2/options/0: You see more, but objects get smaller and the edges distort, like a wide-angle lens
cards/3/task: The blue cube is far away and has disappeared. Fix it without touching fov or the camera position.
cards/4/q: Why did the blue cube disappear?
cards/4/options/0: It is 20 units away and far = 10: anything beyond far gets cut off
cards/4/explain: far is the back wall of the view frustum.
cards/5/body: Three.js has no built-in units: 1 is just 1. But glTF and physics engines agree that 1 = 1 meter, and it pays to stick with that: lights and shadows are tuned for that scale.
cards/6/q: Match each parameter to its meaning
cards/7/q: A camera with a 60° angle that sees from 0.1 to 1000
cards/7/explain: near = 0 is not allowed. More on that in the next lesson.
cards/8/q: The fov of a PerspectiveCamera is the angle…
cards/8/explain: The horizontal angle is derived from the vertical one and aspect.
